adversarialReview.secondMechanismConsidered (ENFORCEMENT.m: The first full run of pe-subscription.test.ts (13 tests) showed 12 passed and 1 failed with 'Hook timed out in 30000ms' on the FIRST test's afterEach (truncateAll across ~150 tables, right after createTestSchema replayed a 5097-line DDL template into a freshly-created local Docker postgres container with no prior cache warmth). Considered whether this was a defect in the route or in my test's interaction with the shared afterEach hook. Rejected: (a) every other test in the same run, including tests AFTER the failing one, passed with normal 5-10s timing; (b) a second, unmodified re-run of the identical file against the same running container passed all 13/13, the previously-slow first test included, at normal (~6s) speed; (c) nothing about my route or test writes to any of the ~150 truncated tables beyond users/pe_user_entitlements, which is a subset every other passing test in the file also touched. The explanation that survives is first-run cold-start cost specific to this local ad hoc Docker Postgres instance (schema replay + orphan-schema reap, done once), not a property of the code under test -- consistent with the environment declaration below.

environmentForThisInstrument: DATABASE_URL/postgres was NOT present in this fresh clone/worktree (test-env.ts deliberately leaves it untouched, per its own comment, expecting an external provisioner). CI (.github/workflows/pr-checks.yml, Test job) provisions pgvector/pgvector:pg14 with postgres/postgres/test_db on 5432, then installs postgresql-14-postgis-3 via apt inside the container and CREATE EXTENSION vector + postgis, before running tests -- both extensions are load-bearing: grep of lib/db/src/__tests__/__fixtures__/schema.sql.template shows 8 postgis/geometry references and 1 vector(...) column, so the shared DDL replay fails without them regardless of which tables a given test touches. Replicated the identical setup locally: `docker run -d --name p129-pe-subscription-testdb -e POSTGRES_USER=postgres -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -e POSTGRES_DB=test_db -p 55611:5432 pgvector/pgvector:pg14`, then `CREATE EXTENSION vector`, then `apt-get install -y postgresql-14-postgis-3` inside the container (root, exit 0) followed by `CREATE EXTENSION postgis`. Tests run with DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@localhost:55611/test_db, PRIVATE_OBJECT_DIR=/test-bucket/private, PUBLIC_OBJECT_SEARCH_PATHS=/test-bucket/public -- matching pr-checks.yml's Test job env exactly except the port (55611 chosen to avoid an unrelated postgres:15 container already bound to host 5432).
